slot.brief: 4 short sentences (PQRS) on a simple, familiar topic (e.g., daily habit or a well-known fact) with an obvious chronological or pronoun link; ask for the correct PQRS order.

stem:
Arrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph.

P: Neha checks her timetable for the next day's classes.
Q: It tells her which books and notebooks she will need.
R: She places those items in her schoolbag.
S: The bag is ready beside the door, so she can leave promptly in the morning.

Which is the correct sequence?

verdicts.working: P introduces the timetable; Q explains what it indicates; R describes packing those items; S concludes with the ready bag.

working:
“It” in Q refers to the timetable in P. “Those items” in R refers to the books and notebooks identified in Q. S describes the packed bag, so it follows R.

Independent check: P introduces the timetable; Q explains what it indicates; R describes packing those items; S concludes with the ready bag.
solution: P introduces the timetable, which Q explains tells Neha what books and notebooks she needs. R describes packing those items, and S concludes with the ready bag.
